title: A vocabulary floor
statement: When the text supplies a stronger word than an answer uses, treat the answer as unfinished, not wrong: accept it, then push once for the text's word.
example: In one design, a child who writes "nice" where the text says "kindest" is accepted and then asked once for the stronger word.
detail: The closing-questions design requires at least one slot in its finding question to carry the text's own words, calling it the place where vocabulary is either held or lost (`grade3-reading/artifacts/feedback-closing-questions-2026-09-24/Closing_Questions_Pattern.txt`). An answer in weaker words than the text supplies is unfinished, not wrong: it is accepted, then pushed once for the stronger word the text gives, and the rule is repeated as a floor for all three closing questions.
